_comment: Filename slugs: the byte-for-byte agreement between the app and the brain.
Two writers share every config store. The desktop's fileUtils.ts (slugLibrary,
slugLayout, slugSession) and the Go brain's cmd/brain/slug.go decide the
on-disk NAME for library.save, layouts.save and sessions.save, and either one
can answer depending on DELEGATE_CATALOG_TO_BRAIN. slug.go's own header says
it is 'a Go port of fileUtils.ts slug() ... so the brain writes and deletes the
exact same filenames the app does', and layoutService.ts says its path rule
'mirrors layoutFilePath in cmd/brain/stores.go rule for rule'. Nothing enforced
either claim: fileUtils.test.ts and stores_test.go each tested their own copy,
which is exactly how the divergence below survived.
THE DIVERGENCE, and the reason this fixture exists. Case folding is not the
same operation in the two languages. Go's strings.ToLower is a per-rune simple
fold; JavaScript's String.prototype.toLowerCase is the full Unicode SPECIAL
CASING mapping, which can make a string LONGER. U+0130 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I
WITH DOT ABOVE is the one that bites: Go folds it to a single 'i', JS folds it
to 'i' + U+0307 COMBINING DOT ABOVE, and the combining mark is then a bad
character and becomes a '-'. So a layout named 'aİb' was written as aib.yaml
with id 'aib' by the brain and as ai-b.yaml with id 'ai-b' by the app — same
store, two writers, two filenames. The item is then invisible to the other
provider's list, and delete re-slugs and unlinks a name that was never written,
so it cannot be removed. (U+212A KELVIN SIGN is the mirror case: both used to
fold it to 'k'.)
THE RULE, now shared: lowercase ASCII A-Z ONLY, then apply the variant's
charset. Every character the two implementations could disagree about is
non-ASCII, and every non-ASCII character is replaced by '-' by all three
variants anyway — so restricting the fold costs nothing a caller could want and
removes the entire class of disagreement, including the ones no corpus has
thought of yet. It changes the output only for inputs that fold ACROSS the
ASCII boundary, i.e. U+0130 (already divergent, so nothing consistent existed
to preserve) and U+212A (a bad character in both now, where both used to fold it
to 'k').
VARIANTS. `library`: collapse runs of bad chars into one '-', trim all
leading/trailing dashes, no length cap, fallback 'item'. `layout`: single-char
replace then dedup runs, trim, cap 64, fallback 'layout'. `session`: same as
layout but NO dash trimming and no fallback (empty in, empty out). The caps are
counted the same way on both sides because the output alphabet is ASCII, so a
byte cap and a code-unit cap coincide — a property that only holds because the
fold above runs first.
LOADERS: apps/desktop/src/main/lib/fileUtils.test.ts and
services/hub/cmd/brain/slug_test.go. Both must run every case for all three
variants; `expect` carries one string per variant.
THE BLOCK REGISTRY. Every array-of-objects block in this file must be declared
here and everything here must be a block — closure in both directions, so a new
block is a failure until someone says what its cases must carry, and a renamed
one cannot quietly stop being validated.
Held by cmd/brain/corpusvocab_test.go and
apps/desktop/src/main/services/contractsVocabulary.test.ts. Before those, this
kind of validation existed for exactly ONE block of ONE fixture.

cases.why: One input, one expected slug per variant (library/layout/session).

cases.name: an ordinary title
cases.why: The regression floor. Every real save looks like this and must keep the byte-for-byte filename it has today.

cases.name: already a slug (idempotence)
cases.why: remove() re-slugs a stored id, so slug(slug(x)) must equal slug(x) or an item becomes undeletable — the same failure shape as the U+0130 divergence, from the other direction.

cases.name: underscores and digits survive
cases.why: The allowed alphabet is [a-z0-9_-] in every variant; a copy that dropped '_' would rename every existing file that has one.

cases.name: a run of bad characters
cases.why: The two charset variants differ in HOW they collapse (one pass over runs vs. single-char replace then dedup) and must still agree on the answer.

cases.name: leading and trailing punctuation
cases.why: The one place the variants legitimately differ: session does NOT trim dashes. Pinning it here stops a well-meaning unification from renaming every saved session file.

cases.name: nothing but punctuation
cases.why: Three different fallbacks — 'item', 'layout', and none at all. A shared helper that picked one would break two call sites.

cases.name: the empty string
cases.why: sessionService relies on empty-in/empty-out; the other two must produce their fallback rather than an empty filename.

cases.name: uppercase ASCII folds
cases.why: The floor for the narrowed fold: restricting case folding to ASCII must not stop ASCII from folding.

cases.name: U+0130 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE, inside a word
cases.why: THE DIVERGENCE. Go folded it to 'i' and answered 'aib'; JS folded it to 'i' + U+0307 and answered 'ai-b'. Under catalog delegation the brain wrote <configDir>/layouts/aib.yaml while the app wrote ai-b.yaml, so the item was invisible to the other provider's list and its delete unlinked a name that was never written. Now both treat it as the non-ASCII character it is.

cases.name: U+0130 alone
cases.why: The session variant made it worse than the layout one because it does not trim: Go said 'i' and JS said 'i-'. With the shared fold both see a single bad character.

cases.name: U+0130 after a dash
cases.why: Go '-i' vs JS '-i-'. Included because it is the case where the two answers differ in LENGTH as well as content, which is what makes the two files impossible to reconcile after the fact.

cases.name: U+212A KELVIN SIGN
cases.why: The mirror of U+0130: both languages used to fold it INTO ASCII ('kelvin'), so this is the one input the narrowed fold deliberately changes. Recorded as a decision, not an accident — a character that renders as a unit symbol is not a 'K', and the two copies agreeing is worth more than either answer.

cases.name: a Turkish dotless i is an ordinary non-ASCII character
cases.why: Neither language ever folded this one into ASCII, so it pins that the narrowed fold did not accidentally start doing so.

cases.name: accented letters
cases.why: The ordinary non-ASCII case, unchanged by the fold narrowing: both copies already answered this identically and must keep doing so.

cases.name: a multi-byte character next to the length cap
cases.why: Go caps by BYTES (len) and TypeScript by UTF-16 code units (substring). They coincide only because the cap is applied AFTER the alphabet replacement, which leaves pure ASCII — this case fails loudly if anyone ever moves the truncation earlier.

cases.name: a long name is truncated at 64 and re-trimmed
cases.why: library has NO cap; layout and session cap at 64. The cut lands one character before the '-', so it also pins that the re-trim after truncation only fires when it has to.

cases.name: truncation that lands on a dash is re-trimmed
cases.why: 63 a's, then the cut falls exactly on the '-'. layout re-trims it (or slug stops being idempotent and layouts become undeletable, the bug the re-trim was added for); session does not trim at all and keeps it.
